title: Market Rivalry Drives Investment: A New Framework
discussion_signal: The public research translation connects product-market rivalry to aggregate investment and capital allocation, while emphasizing heterogeneous markup and concentration responses to cost-of-capital shocks. It also flags a modest decline in aggregate capital formation among merging firms since 1995, making industrial investment and consumer competition a joint question.
linked_research_question: How do product-market rivalry, financing conditions, mergers, markups, and concentration jointly change firm investment and downstream consumer or worker outcomes?
limits: The post summarizes a structural model and US public-company evidence
Firm-level markup and investment responses are heterogeneous and do not automatically establish consumer harm
Selected LinkedIn discussion cannot establish market prevalence or causal welfare effects
